answer: A customer must inform the bank about an unauthorized electronic transaction within three working days to have zero liability [D021, p.30].
The bank must resolve a customer's complaint about an unauthorized electronic banking transaction within 90 days. [D146, p.34]
The bank must credit the amount involved in an unauthorized transaction within 10 working days from the date of such notification by the customer [D126, p.42].
The bank must activate an inoperative account within three working days while following the KYC guidelines [D146, p.15].
When a customer reports a system-level unauthorized transaction after a delay of four to seven working days, the maximum liability for a BSBD account is ₹5,000 [D145, p.30].
The maximum liability for credit cards with a limit above Rs 5 lakh in the same delayed-reporting case is ₹25,000 [D021, p.29].
